hero.heading: A 360° Approach to Sonic Storytelling
hero.line: Music production, sound design and everything around it, from the first idea to the final mix.

intro.question: What do Nina Chuba, The Backstreet Boys and a secret lab in the Alps have in common? Let’s find out.

spots.text: Some projects call for all-round production, like when we worked with Nina Chuba on this Samsung spot. We took her voice recordings from the film set and created a fitting soundtrack for the visuals, some subtle SFX to support the movement of the spot and an overall natural yet hi-end mix to round out the project.

But the talent doesn’t always have to be musical. For the relaunch of the Schwarzkopf brand, we composed a brand song with changing arrangements to suit a variety of celebrities and influencers including Diane Kruger, Collien Fernandes, Sofia Vergara, Ana Ivanović and Alli Neumann to name a few (oh wait, Alli actually is a musician, but you get the drift). Here’s the hero version.

Sometimes the artist is in the spotlight, but for this VW campaign, the talent was hiding in the background. For the launch of the VW e-up! we created this fresh beat and had UK Grime legend Che Lingo work his magic on it. “They never thought we were good enough, now we’re pullin’ up…”

A song doesn’t always have to be the main focus though. For this Gore-Tex campaign we went into their secret testing facility in the Bavarian Alps and recorded all of their weird and wonderful all-weather testing machines, turning them into this epic adventure in sound design.
Sound design can be adventurous, sound design can be subtle and sound design can also be insane, like when you’re hyped up on too many energy drinks.

We didn’t write this song (obviously), but instead remade this Backstreet Boys classic with a group of “singers” who should maybe stick to acting. But that was part of the fun, as was creating the overall sound design and mix of the spot.

Earlier we remade the Backstreet Boys, now we’re remaking Michael Sembello’s 80s classic, Maniac. From licensing, to recreating those legendary 80s synth sounds to casting a singer who can hit the (very) high notes like it’s the most normal thing in the world, we had it “covered” from start to finish.
Phew… need to calm down a little after that one. How about a lovely little heart-warming, nostalgic, acoustic ballad to bring down the pulse and remind us of the sweeter moments in life?

We do like to get more artistic too from time to time, like in this cinematic Adidas Superstar spot featuring rapper Jugo Ürdens and shot on 16mm. The music sounds like a film score from yesteryear and we felt nostalgic recording brass, woodwinds and grand piano for it, before creating the sound design and final mix.
To sum it all up… we love all things music and all things audio. Here’s one last spot with lots of different styles and sounds in it, because you can combine metal with salsa and trap if you want to.

services.heading: Sonic Strategy
services.line: Your brand needs a Sonic Identity – but which one?
services.intro: We analyze your brand, its cultural context, the sounds of the market, and the habits of your target audience to define your perfect sonic identity. These are our tools:

items.name: Sonic Sweetspot
items.text: With our Sonic Sweetspot service, we provide a robust brand and competitor analysis that identifies the distinctive musical space a brand can claim for itself within the market.

items.name: Sonic Trend Radar
items.text: Our Sonic Trend Radar service gathers information on emerging sonic trends relevant to your brand, and suggests creative ways in which you can capitalize on their cultural impact.

items.name: ArtistMatch
items.text: Our ArtistMatch service uses both data-based research alongside qualitative factors to ensure the artist partnerships we recommend are not only creatively inspired but feel authentic and make strategic sense.

services.heading: Content Production
services.line: How do we bring your sonic identity to life?
services.intro: From strategy to real life. Informed by our analytical insights, we craft all kinds of assets shaped by music culture - from sound and film to events, merch, digital content, and immersive experiences - to power your communication across every touchpoint.

items.name: Sonic Branding & Identity
items.text: We don’t create jingles. We build sonic identities that become cultural signatures. Your sound is not decoration. It’s your brand’s heartbeat — recognizable, emotional, unforgettable.

items.name: Content & Campaign Production
items.text: We design campaigns, social content, films, and brand experiences that don’t just grab attention — they earn emotional loyalty. Every piece of content starts with your sonic DNA and turns it into real-world resonance.

items.name: Cultural Activation & Experiences
items.text: We orchestrate artist collaborations, branded playlists, cultural partnerships, and live experiences that make your brand part of the conversation — not an outsider shouting from the sidelines.

services.heading: Performance & Measurement
services.intro: Keen insights and extraordinary craft are only part of the story. None of it means anything if we can’t measure the impact of our actions. We provide reporting, market research and data analytics to empirically prove the efficacy of our sonic strategies.
services.alt: Sonic Strategy Score in the Sonic Performance Tracker dashboard

items.name: Direct Response Tracking
items.text: We measure what matters immediately: engagement rates, shares, searches, and audience reactions across platforms. No assumptions. Just clear signals that your sound is being heard — and felt.

items.name: Cultural Resonance Analysis
items.text: We track how your activations resonate emotionally and culturally — across demographics, subcultures, and digital spaces. Because cultural relevance isn’t built on views. It’s built on meaning.

items.name: Strategic Impact Scoring
items.text: Our Cultural Relevance Score and Strategy Score reveal how music drives brand loyalty, emotional equity, and market leadership. Finally, creativity you can manage — and monetize.

Wenn Sie uns per E-Mail oder Telefon kontaktieren, wird Ihre Anfrage inklusive aller daraus hervorgehenden personenbezogenen Daten (Name, Anfrage) zum Zwecke der Bearbeitung Ihres Anliegens bei uns gespeichert und verarbeitet. Diese Daten geben wir nicht ohne Ihre Einwilligung weiter.

Die Verarbeitung dieser Daten erfolgt auf Grundlage von Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. b DSGVO, sofern Ihre Anfrage mit der Erfüllung eines Vertrags zusammenhängt oder zur Durchführung vorvertraglicher Maßnahmen erforderlich ist. In allen übrigen Fällen beruht die Verarbeitung auf unserem berechtigten Interesse an der effektiven Bearbeitung der an uns gerichteten Anfragen (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. f DSGVO) oder auf Ihrer Einwilligung (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. a DSGVO) sofern diese abgefragt wurde; die Einwilligung ist jederzeit widerrufbar.

Die von Ihnen an uns per Kontaktanfragen übersandten Daten verbleiben bei uns, bis Sie uns zur Löschung auffordern, Ihre Einwilligung zur Speicherung widerrufen oder der Zweck für die Datenspeicherung entfällt (z. B. nach abgeschlossener Bearbeitung Ihres Anliegens). Zwingende gesetzliche Bestimmungen – insbesondere gesetzliche Aufbewahrungsfristen – bleiben unberührt.

Willkommens-Video und Speicherung im Browser

Beim ersten Besuch zeigen wir ein kurzes Video über unsere Arbeit. Das Video laden wir von unserem eigenen Cloud-Speicher (siehe „Videos und Audiodateien“).

Wenn Sie das Video schließen oder ansehen, speichert Ihr Browser einen einfachen Vermerk („bereits gesehen“) im lokalen Speicher (Local Storage). So erscheint das Video nicht bei jedem Besuch erneut. Solange Sie nichts davon tun, wird nichts gespeichert. Wir setzen dafür kein Cookie.

Der Vermerk enthält keine Kennung und keine personenbezogenen Daten. Er wird nicht an uns oder Dritte übertragen. Er bleibt gespeichert, bis Sie ihn in Ihren Browsereinstellungen löschen.

Rechtsgrundlage ist § 25 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 TDDDG. Die Speicherung ist unbedingt erforderlich, damit sich die Website merkt, dass Sie das Video bereits geschlossen oder gesehen haben.
